key_insight: Physics-informed synthetic histories can warm-start PV time-series foundation models and deliver strong zero-shot forecasting before any site measurements exist.
engineering_relevance: This enables commissioning-time PV production forecasting for new plants, supporting grid planning and operational decisions in cold-start deployments.
method: Generate a synthetic PV production history from plant metadata and meteorological covariates.
Feed the synthetic history into time-series foundation models via inference-time conditioning.
Benchmark five TSFMs against classical baselines under Cold-Start Baseline, Real Feedback, and Self-Forecast Feedback settings.
evidence_signal: Across 440 PV sites in four datasets, covariate-aware foundation models outperformed baselines by about 1.7–2×, with TabPFN-TS best under Real Feedback and Chronos-2 most robust under Self-Forecast Feedback.
watch_item: Results suggest performance depends more on having plausible temporal context than on the exact synthetic-history generator, so deployment quality may be sensitive to how realistic the generated history is.
paper_title: Time series Foundation Models based on Physics-Informed Synthetic Histories for Cold-Start Photovoltaic Forecasting
